before.title: Energy flow in crossed external fields with finite-volume accounting
before.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the transverse faces carry the fluxes $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0E_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.

before.physical_scope: The explicit ideal source-free travelling plane-wave configuration $E=E_0\cos(kz-\omega t)e_1$, $B=(E_0/c)\cos(kz-\omega t)e_2$, $\omega=ck$, as a worked example of the vacuum energy density and Poynting vector and of the local and finite-box energy accounting of the electromagnetic energy balance.
